newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan minister says telecom sale must wait.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan minister says telecom sale must wait.

text.p: Pakistan's Communications Minister Azam Hoti said on Monday that state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation (PTCL) would not be privatised unless its financial position improved.
Hoti told the National Assembly (lower house) that the former government led by Benazir Bhutto had sold 11.8 percent of PTCL's shares, but taken no steps to improve its finances.
"Unless the situation improves to a great extent, the government will not privatise the PTCL," the official news agency APP quoted Hoti as saying.

Confusion has reigned over prospects for the much-delayed sale of a 26 percent stake in PTCL to a strategic investor since Hoti was quoted as saying on Friday that the plan had been postponed because of the utility's heavy liabilities.

A spokesman for the Privatisation Commission said on Sunday the sale was still on the government's "active agenda" and described the impression that it had been postponed indefinitely as "totally incorrect and misleading."

"Soon after the financial accounts of PTCL are finalised and published, the company will be processed for privatisation and shortly a definite programme for the privatisation of PTCL will be announced," the spokesman said.
